caveats: This is a logical-resource extrapolation. It has not been simulated and has certainly not been executed on hardware.
Grover iterations are inherently serial: the total depth figure is a single sequential circuit, not something that parallelises away. Distributing the search over m machines buys only sqrt(m).

Real attack costs are evaluated under a depth cap (NIST's MAXDEPTH). Under any plausible cap the full iteration count cannot be run, and the effective security is higher than the query count suggests.
No error correction is included. Every T gate here is a logical T requiring a distilled magic state; see the physical estimator for what that implies under an explicit hardware model.
Assumes a unique preimage and an idealised oracle success probability; real preimage search over a 256-bit digest with a shorter message has a different solution-density structure.

assumptions: Surface code with a 0.01 threshold and the standard p_L = 0.1 (p/p_th)^((d+1)/2) error fit (Fowler et al., arXiv:1208.0928).
Physical error rate p = 0.0001, code cycle 1e-07 s.
Physical qubits per logical qubit = 2 d^2, covering the data patch plus routing space.
16 magic-state factory/factories, 10 code cycles per T state, 100,000 physical qubits each. Published factory designs vary by more than an order of magnitude; these are inputs, not findings.
Total failure probability budget 0.01 for the whole circuit.
Connectivity assumed 2D nearest-neighbour; the logical circuit's depth was measured assuming all-to-all connectivity, so routing overhead is NOT included and the runtime here is optimistic.
T-count comes from the standard Toffoli decomposition; a different decomposition changes this estimate.
This is a model, not a prediction. No hardware was involved at any point.
